A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPDIM research, with matching central methods, datasets, and retained results. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations and motor-imagery and sleep-staging experiments in Sections 4.1–4.3, with results in Figures 2–3, Tables 1–2, and the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and reports additional baseline comparisons and simulation sensitivity experiments in Tables A2–A5 and Figures A1–A4.

M1.justification: The operational SPDIM method remains unchanged: domain recentering, the SPD bias and geodesic parameterizations, information-maximization loss, and adaptation with the feature extractor and classifier fixed. Expanded architecture and optimization descriptions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four motor-imagery datasets, CAP, Dreem, HMC, ISRUC, and synthetic binary classification. Cross-session/cross-subject transfer and balanced/shifted conditions already occur in v1. The added simulation sweeps vary configurations within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated EA and STMA comparisons, DeepSleepNet and AttnSleep for sleep staging, and EEGNet v4, EEG-Conformer, ATCNet, and EEGInceptionMI for motor imagery (Tables A2, A4–A5). This substantially broadens external benchmarking. The former TSMNet+RCT rows match TSMNet+SPDDSBN and are not new comparators.

E3.justification: The simulation design expands to controlled sweeps of source-domain counts, 100–800 samples per domain, covariance dimensions 2/4/8, and 1–3 informative dimensions. Appendix A6 also specifies two informative dimensions where v1 Section 4.1 specified one; this is a reported setting revision without establishing reruns. Existing real-EEG preprocessing and cross-validation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Figures A1–A4 test sensitivity to source-domain count, sample availability, covariance dimensionality, and informative dimensions, substantially extending the original separability/label-ratio analysis. These reveal conditions where adaptation becomes less reliable. The sleep-staging ablation scores in v4 Table A3 were already present in v1 Table A2 and are reorganized rather than new.

E5.justification: Figure 3 newly identifies error bars as 95% confidence intervals; v1's caption referred to standard deviations in brackets. Reported multiple-testing families change, including 4 to 14 tests in Table 1 and 7 to 14 for shifted motor imagery. The permutation/t-max framework remains, and neither version supplies repeat-run counts or seeds. v4's sleep-table captions inconsistently state 14 versus 10 tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive baseline scores and simulation sensitivity results, while retaining original SPDIM scores, including 73.5%/69.9% for healthy/patient sleep groups and 77.5%/68.5% for shifted cross-session/cross-subject motor imagery. New comparisons qualify superiority: Table A2 reports AttnSleep+STMA at 74.6% on ISRUC patients versus SPDIM's 71.6%. These are expanded findings, not an improvement in SPDIM's retained scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly assumes that B is sparse and structured so label information occupies the first D-dimensional block of log(E). This narrows the formal generative specification. Propositions 1–2 and their appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged; other mathematical edits mainly simplify notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statement, and discussion retain the same central claims: a generative explanation of conditional and label shifts, limitations of recentering under label shifts, and parameter-efficient SPDIM adaptation. Expanded supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds a specific limitation: noise and outliers can make IM estimate a bias in the wrong direction and increase variability. Section 4.3 additionally interprets domainwise centering as harmful relative to global centering under label shifts and introduces a limited qualification concerning TSMNet+STMA.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies full-target gradient estimation and 50 adaptation epochs, and Appendix A7 documents TSMNet layers, filter counts, eigenvalue rectification, model selection, and sleep-baseline implementation and training choices. These materially expand reproducibility information. Existing source-training optimizer settings, batch sizes, and hardware descriptions are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v4 adds alignment references including Collas et al. (2024), Ju and Guan (2022), and Gnassounou et al. (2024), plus architecture and sleep-model references. These broaden the surrounding context and support the added comparisons without substantially changing the paper's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall section sequence remain. v4 reorganizes training/adaptation descriptions, moves implementation material into expanded appendices, rewrites portions of the experimental discussion, and standardizes terminology and class-prior notation. These are localized editorial and structural revisions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is comprehensively redesigned around generation, source training, and target adaptation. Table 2 becomes a component-based ablation display; appendix comparisons are expanded and separated into dedicated tables. Four sensitivity figures are added, Figure 2 gains separability annotations, and Figure 3 is relocated and relabeled.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially addresses v1's narrow external benchmarking and limited sensitivity evidence through Tables A2/A4–A5 and Figures A1–A4. Added implementation details and an explicit failure mechanism also make the work easier to reproduce and assess. These gains outweigh reporting shortcomings: Section 4.3 still overstates significant superiority despite unmarked comparisons in Table A2, and the sleep-table captions disagree on testing-family size. The improvement comes from stronger scrutiny and documentation, not higher retained scores.
